<thought>Examining the mass spectrum, the most distinctive feature is a strong M+2 peak (≈24 % of the base peak) at m/z 235.96, which matches the natural abundance ratio of ^37Cl to ^35Cl (≈24 % / 76 %). No comparable M+2 pattern is seen for bromine (which would be ~1:1) or sulfur (which would be only ~4 % per S atom). Thus chlorine can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution. The regular 1 Da spacing indicates carbon isotopes, but carbon is ubiquitous and not uniquely identifiable from this pattern alone. Therefore, the only element that can be definitively identified is chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['Cl']</final_answer>
